Commentary.Commentary: We are back with the chase. The umpires and the players are all out in the middle. Sanjana Kavindi and Sumudu Nisansala are the openers for Sri Lanka Women Under-19. Shabnam has the new ball in hand and will start the proceedings. Away we go!
... THE RUN CHASE ...

What truly stood out for Sri Lanka Women Under-19, apart from their impressive spin attack, was their electric fielding. Barring one minor lapse, they were sharp and relentless, making life difficult for the Indian batters. While 119 might not appear to be a daunting target, the pitch offers plenty of assistance for spinners, and India’s red-hot bowling attack will undoubtedly test Sri Lanka’s resolve. An exciting second half is on the horizon so stay tuned to see how this thrilling contest unfolds!

Trisha Gongadi is in for a chat. She says that this is a good total and they are confident of defending it. Tells that the wicket is on the slower side and wasn't the easiest wicket to bat. Mentions that she waited for the ball to come to her. Backs her bowlers to defend the total.

Aseni Thalagune claiming the wicket of the Indian skipper proved pivotal, as no batter thereafter managed to settle against Sri Lanka’s spin-dominant attack. Trisha Gongadi, who looked set for a well-deserved half-century, fell just one run short, triggering a collapse. Mithila Vinod and Joshitha V J chipped in with some crucial runs toward the end, but India were ultimately restricted to a modest 118.

Trisha got off to a promising start, and just as India seemed to be finding some momentum, Pramudi Methsara turned the tide by striking twice in a single over, mounting the pressure on the Indians. The rain interruption provided India with a much-needed opportunity to reassess their plans, and it started to pay off when Trisha and skipper Niki Prasad returned to the crease with a renewed approach. The runs began to flow, but Sri Lanka’s bowlers regrouped admirably to wrest back control.

A brilliant effort from the Sri Lankan bowlers ensures that India finish their innings at 118 runs. While the pitch hasn’t been the easiest to bat on, Sri Lanka will be delighted with their disciplined performance and will fancy their chances of chasing this target down.

Commentary.Commentary: Drinks! Sri Lanka Women Under-19 have struck at just the right moment, breaking the partnership and creating an opportunity to pile more pressure on the Indians. Trisha Gongadi has been in sublime touch, effortlessly accumulating runs, but with her partner back in the pavilion, she’ll now rely on Bhavika to provide some support and stitch a big partnership. Sri Lanka, on the other hand, will be well aware that this Indian middle-order hasn’t been tested in the tournament so far. They will have to look to launch an all-out attack to exploit this chance.

PITCH REPORT - Ed Rainsford is near the deck. He says that the clouds look ominous and it has gotten a lot cooler. Tells that spinners have dominated at this venue in 10 innings so far with 43 wickets falling to spin as compared to the 16 against pace. Adds that out of the 43 wickets, 33 have fallen in the middle phase - overs 7-15. Mentions that the batters will have to be smart with their options against spin. Feels that given the overhead conditions, there will be something in it for the pacers as well.
Niki Prasad, the skipper of India says they will try to put up a good score. Mentions that they are very confident and will look to give their best again. Says they go unchanged too.

The captain of Sri Lanka, Manudi Nanayakkara says that with with the weather around, they want to bowl first. Tells that they had a good last game and want to keep up the momentum. Informs that they are going unchanged.

In the earlier game of the day at this venue, West Indies defeated the tournament hosts, Malaysia, convincingly. The West Indies' dominant performance secured them a spot in the Super Six stage, joining Sri Lanka and India as the three teams progressing from Group A. While the West Indies are set to finish as the third-placed team in the group, the coveted top spot is still up for grabs, and it will be decided through this clash between India and Sri Lanka.

Sri Lanka Women Under-19, on the other hand, have relied heavily on their batting to dominate games, securing two convincing victories. Spin spearhead Chamudi Praboda has been their standout performer with the ball, but the rest of the bowling unit will need to step up significantly to counter India’s strong lineup. While both teams have already secured their spots in the Super Sixes, this game carries significant importance as points and net run rates will carry forward into the next stage. The toss and team updates are just moments away, so stay tuned for what promises to be a thrilling contest!

Defending champions India have been in scintillating form, delivering commanding performances with both bat and ball. Their bowlers, particularly the spinners, have been instrumental in dismantling opponents, while the pacers have impressed with the new ball as well. The batting unit hasn’t been tested much, as India’s modest chases in both games have been clinical. However, this match might provide an opportunity for the Indian batters to fine-tune ahead of the Super Six stage.

The final game of group-stage action at the 2025 ICC Women's Under-19 T20 World Cup sees defending champions India facing Sri Lanka at the Bayuemas Oval in Kuala Lumpur. Both teams have remained unbeaten so far in Group A, with dominant victories over West Indies and Malaysia, securing their spots in the Super Six stage. However, this encounter holds crucial significance as the winner will top the group. This not only helps avoid a potential Super Six showdown against the winner of Group D but also, since teams carry forward both their wins and net run rate against fellow qualifiers from the group, a victory here will provide a vital advantage in the next round. India’s victories so far have been achieved while chasing modest targets of 45 and 32, meaning their batters have not yet been fully tested. The top order of Trisha Gongadi, Kamalini G, and Sanika Chalke has had some time in the middle, albeit brief, and could come good against a strong Lankan side. India's bowling has been a key strength, particularly their slow left-arm orthodox spinners. Vaishnavi Sharma, on debut, was exceptional against Malaysia, with figures of 5 for 5, including a hat-trick. With as many as four options available, the defending champions rotated their attack in the previous game, bringing in Sharma for Sonam Yadav. It remains to be seen whether they will rotate again or stick with the same spin combination for this crucial match against Sri Lanka. As for Sri Lanka, both of their wins have come while batting first, which has allowed them to get a solid understanding of how to pace their innings across the full 20 overs. The confidence gained from having runs on the board, particularly from key players like Sanjana Kavindi, Dahami Sanethma, and captain Manudi Nanayakkara, could provide Sri Lanka with the edge going into this crucial encounter. Like India, Sri Lanka have also relied on spin, with 15-year-old left-arm spinner Chamudi Praboda being the standout performer so far. However, to overcome a power-packed Indian batting unit, it will take more than just individual brilliance. Sri Lanka will need collective contributions from their bowlers, with the likes of Shashini Gimhani, Limansa Thilakaratne, and Aseni Thalagune expected to step up and deliver. These two sides faced off during the Asia Cup at the same venue in December last year, where India came out on top. Can Sri Lanka turn the tables this time and clinch victory in this crucial encounter? We shall find out.
